projects.title: Visa Design AI Enablement
description: The Visa Design AI Enablement platform is an internal tool built to help Visa designers and developers leverage the power of Generative AI (GenAI) with our embedded design offerings in their workflows. The platform provides a suite of tools and integrations that allow users to generate code snippets, design assets, and documentation using state-of-the-art AI models. By integrating these capabilities into the existing design and development processes, the platform aims to enhance productivity, foster creativity, and streamline project workflows across the organization.

My role on this project was to lead the backend architecture and development of the platform. This involved designing and implementing a robust and scalable backend infrastructure using Express.js, MongoDB, Python, and PostgreSQL. I was responsible for integrating various AI models and services, ensuring seamless communication between the frontend and backend components, and implementing features such as vector search for efficient retrieval of AI-generated content. Additionally, I worked closely with the frontend team to ensure a smooth user experience and collaborated with stakeholders to gather requirements and deliver a product that meets the needs of Visa's design and development teams. The platform has been instrumental in accelerating design and development processes, enabling teams to leverage AI-generated content for various applications, including code generation, automated documentation, and chatbot development. Our VPDS (Visa Product Design System) MCP Server (Model Context Protocol) is also integrated to facilitate context-aware interactions with AI models, enhancing the relevance and accuracy of generated content by loading context from the design system matching the project's needs.

My involvement on the project started since before it was fully chartered, by simply curating the documentation data and developing a prototype of the backend services that could support remote consumption of the data for our main portal (https://design.visa.com) as well as AI integrations for design and development workflow. We built multiple prototypes, tested them, gathered feedback and adapted our project to build our alpha and final platform generalized to all design assets across Visa including Design guidelines, Content standards, Accessibility requirements, and Code libraries including Angular, React, Styles (HTML+CSS), Flutter, and Data Visualization charts.

projects.title: Visa Product Design System
description: The Visa Product Design System (VPDS) is a public design system focused on serving applications with Visa-ready design mocks, design patterns, styles, and components. We've divided VPDS into different tracks to support multiple technologies and methods of consumption. These tracks include Design, Web (HTML + CSS), Angular, React, and Flutter, Accessibility, and Content. The project was also set up as an internally open-sourced project, in which many designers and developers across the company could contribute to the design system.

My role on this projects was to lead the Web libraries, and architect the CSS library. These responsibilities included pixel-perfect styles implemention and enabling configurable theming with high customization options. We also provide documentation with accessible HTML snippets for markup reference and customization guidance. In a way, this worked like an internal bootstrap and tailwind library with responsive behavior and with accessibility (a11y) testing across browsers and screen readers. The styles exported by have more than 290,000 internal installs consumed by server-side rendered applications, AEM sites (like Visa Developer Center) as well as Angular, React, and other Javascript based applications across the company, including CyberSource and Authorize.NET. All our libraries have been installed more than 615,000 times internally across technologies and versions.

My involvement on the project started since before it was fully chartered, by developing a library of basic components that could be themed, modified, extended, and/or forked to produce other component libraries for multiple projects across Visa. We would provide a default Visa theme, that would then turn into the VPDS design and code libraries. These libraries would also follow Visa's General A11y Guidelines (VGAR) to ensure our components where usable and accessible across the board.
I was the initial developer of the library, and the team has grown to include multiple engineers, designers, accessibility experts, and content designers across Visa in the span of 8+ years.

projects.title: gulp-axe-cli
description: Other axe-based plugins are built to generate reports. While these reports are great for analysis, these CLIs, plugins, and packages do not always work well with development pipelines. With gulp-axe-cli, we leverage the power of gulp as a task runner 💪 and the automation for a11y testing of aXe 💥 to prevent bad code from being committed or built. 👍

projects.title: Perspective
description: Perspective is a company and a product which focuses on tracking and analyzing real time customer reactions to your application. Our customers would create a survey and each question would be triggered and displayed to the user after they performed an action. This would allow the questions to be contextual (relative to the context of the action the user had performed), thus providing a less intrusive user experience by limiting distractions, and improving response rates. All of this aggregated data resulted in visualizations with statistical analysis that would help you understand your users better, finding patterns in their collective responses.

My role was to oversee the development of all the technologies that made Perspective operational, including the marketing site, the plugin for client's apps, the dashboard front-end application, and the API & database updates. I would also oversee visual, application, and UX design, as well as the research and development of our data analytics and visualization.

My involvement on the project when my co-founder and I realized the need for a product like this. We built multiple prototypes, tested them, gathered feedback and market validation, and adapted our project to build our alphas and final beta application.
